title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Opus 5 shipped Friday (Jul 24) — near-Fable-5 intelligence at half the price, now the Max default
bullets.summary: Opus 5 lands with a 1M-token context, up to 128K output, adaptive thinking on by default and a five-level effort ladder; Anthropic says it approaches Fable 5's intelligence at half the price ($5/$25 per M tok), sets a new Anthropic SOTA on Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA, and becomes the default on Claude Max / strongest on Pro. Ships with two beta Platform features: mid-conversation tool changes (swap tools without invalidating the prompt cache) and automatic API fallbacks.
bullets.how: This is the model layer the whole Construct fleet runs on; Opus 5 is the new price/performance default to standardize the agents on, and mid-conversation tool changes map directly onto our long-running scan loops that add/drop connectors mid-run without paying to rebuild the cache. The Anthropic drop the morning board under-weighted.

bullets.title: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless spec is now 2 days out — the breaking rewrite ratifies Tuesday
bullets.summary: The final spec publishes Jul 28 and removes the session handshake, so a remote MCP server can sit behind a plain round-robin load balancer and scale horizontally like any web API; it also brings Extensions/Tasks/MCP Apps, OAuth/OIDC-aligned auth hardening and a formal deprecation policy. Scale context: 10,000+ public MCP servers, 97M+ monthly SDK downloads.
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs is 2 days from a breaking change; the migration + least-authority hardening inventory has to close before Tuesday, and the Tasks extension maps straight onto our long-running scan jobs. Still the load-bearing plumbing action of the week.

bullets.title: arXiv: 'Context Engineering: From Prompts to Corporate Multi-Agent Architecture' (2603.09619)
bullets.summary: Proposes five context-quality criteria — relevance, sufficiency, isolation, economy, provenance — and frames context as the agent's operating system, synthesizing vendor architectures with the academic literature.
bullets.how: A concrete rubric for the exact failure mode our scan agents hit (context bloat over long tool loops); 'economy' and 'isolation' are directly actionable for keeping Lens/Prism/Pulse coherent without dumping everything into one window — the design-side complement to Opus 5's mid-conversation tool changes.

bullets.title: Agent/search funding stays revenue-backed: Perplexity $60M ext at $3.5B (Bezos + NVIDIA), Glean $180M ext
bullets.summary: July saw $1.8B+ across 12+ agent deals, now underwritten by hard metrics (coding agents at $50M+ ARR / 150%+ NRR, enterprise workflow agents closing six-figure F500 contracts) rather than narrative.
bullets.how: Market context, not a tool: it validates PRAGMA's 'AI-operator' thesis that buyers now pay for outcome-backed agents, and sets the bar for how we frame the owned-presence/operator wedge to SMB clients. No build action.

bullets.title: Google's cheaper Gemini line, incl. Gemini 3.6 Flash (Jul 21), holds the low-cost tier
bullets.summary: Google widened the Gemini family with lower-cost tiers aimed at high-volume workloads, 3.6 Flash the newest fast/cheap default.
bullets.how: Keeps the cost/quality split clean for the fleet: cheap Flash for high-volume batch text/image passes, a reasoning tier (now Opus 5) only where it earns its cost; benchmark before rewiring anything load-bearing.

praxis_lesson: The morning board rolled forward on the assumption of 'no new Anthropic drop,' but Friday's Claude Opus 5 was exactly that — a flagship model release, directly load-bearing because it's the layer the fleet runs on, and it should have led from 06:00. The reconcile correction: a same-day re-fire earns no rewrite only when it surfaces already-seated or older items — but a genuine miss of a flagship release always earns the rewrite. The week's throughline holds underneath: standardize the agents on Opus 5 (new default, mid-conversation tool changes), close the Jul-28 stateless-MCP migration + least-authority inventory before Tuesday, and treat context as a governed resource.
